segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have an advanced level lesson for you guys all about food.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为你们提供了关于食物的高级课程。

segments.en: What kind of food are we talking about today, Marco?
segments.zh: 马可，我们今天在谈论什么样的食物？

segments.en: Today we're talking about cheese.
segments.zh: 今天我们谈论的是奶酪。

segments.en: So there's so many different types of cheese, so many varieties.
segments.zh: 所以有这么多不同类型的奶酪，这么多品种。

segments.en: So we're going to take a look at these varieties.
segments.zh: 所以我们要看看这些品种。

segments.en: You may know them or not.
segments.zh: 你可能认识他们或不认识他们。

segments.en: But we're also going to take a look at the pronunciation because most of them are either Italian or French.
segments.zh: 但我们也将看看发音，因为它们中的大多数是意大利语或法语。

segments.en: So how do you pronounce these in maybe in American English?
segments.zh: 那么，您如何用美式英语发音这些？

segments.en: Good question.
segments.zh: 问得好。

segments.en: Let's listen to our dialogue for the first time and we'll be back in a moment to talk about the wonderful world of cheese.
segments.zh: 让我们第一次听我们的对话，我们会在一会儿回来谈论奶酪的美妙世界。

segments.en: Hello everyone.
segments.zh: 大家好。

segments.en: My name is Lori and I want to welcome you to this course.
segments.zh: 我的名字是 Lori，我想欢迎你参加这门课程。

segments.en: We will learn all about one of the oldest yet most delicious foods on this planet, cheese.
segments.zh: 我们将了解这个星球上最古老但最美味的食物之一，奶酪。

segments.en: Let's get started.
segments.zh: 我们开始吧。

segments.en: Cheese is usually categorized into four types, soft, semi-soft, semi-hard, and hard.
segments.zh: 奶酪通常分为四种类型，软，半软，半硬和硬。

segments.en: The designation refers to the amount of moisture in the cheese which directly affects its texture.
segments.zh: 该名称是指奶酪中直接影响其质地的水分量。

segments.en: Making cheese is an ancient practice dating back thousands of years and the home cheese maker can usually find recipes for cheese that fall into any of the four categories.
segments.zh: 制作奶酪是一种古老的做法，可以追溯到数千年前，家庭奶酪制造商通常可以找到属于四类中的任何一种的奶酪食谱。

segments.en: Soft cheese includes cottage cheese, cream cheese, ricotta, brie, blue, roquefort, mozzarella, muenster, and similar cheeses.
segments.zh: 软质奶酪包括茅屋奶酪、奶油奶酪、里科塔乳清奶酪、布里奶酪、蓝纹奶酪、洛克福奶酪、马苏里拉奶酪、芒斯特奶酪等。

segments.en: These cheeses generally pair well with fruit or meats and can be used as breakfast cheeses in an omelet or as pasta fillings.
segments.zh: 这些奶酪通常与水果或肉类搭配得很好，可以用作煎蛋卷中的早餐奶酪或作为意大利面馅料。

segments.en: They are usually mildly flavored and very high in moisture.
segments.zh: 它们通常味道温和，水分非常高。

segments.en: American, Colby, Co-Jack, and similar cheeses are in the semi-soft category.
segments.zh: 美式奶酪、科尔比奶酪、科尔比杰克奶酪等属于半软质奶酪。

segments.en: These are slightly stronger in flavor and cover a wide range of uses.
segments.zh: 它们的味道略强，涵盖了广泛的用途。

segments.en: Co-Jack cheese, a blend of Colby and Monterey Jack, is one of the most popular.
segments.zh: 科尔比杰克奶酪由科尔比奶酪和蒙特雷杰克奶酪混合而成，是最受欢迎的品种之一。

segments.en: This allows the sharper flavor of the Colby to be combined with the milder Jack cheese and also melts better than plain Colby.
segments.zh: 这样就把科尔比奶酪比较浓烈的风味与杰克奶酪较温和的口感融合起来，而且比单独的科尔比奶酪更容易融化。

segments.en: Grilled cheese sandwiches often use American cheese and Mexican cheeses such as asadero and queso fresco are becoming more popular.
segments.zh: 烤奶酪三明治常用美式奶酪；阿萨德罗和鲜奶酪等墨西哥奶酪也越来越受欢迎。

segments.en: Hard cheeses include parmesan, romano, asiago, swiss, gruyere, and others.
segments.zh: 硬质奶酪包括帕尔马干酪、罗马诺奶酪、阿夏戈奶酪、瑞士奶酪和格鲁耶尔奶酪等。

segments.en: Parmesan and romano are most familiar as the grated powder used to top spaghetti, but they are also used as accompaniments for fruit, wine, nuts, and other appetizer items.
segments.zh: 帕尔马干酪和罗马诺奶酪最常见的吃法是磨成粉撒在意大利面上，也可以搭配水果、葡萄酒、坚果及其他开胃小食。

segments.en: Swiss is a popular sandwich cheese and melts well, unlike some other hard cheeses.
segments.zh: 瑞士奶酪常用来做三明治，而且与有些硬质奶酪不同，它很容易融化。

segments.en: Alright we're back, so obviously this is a very interesting lesson because it also gives us an insight on how cheeses are categorized.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，所以显然这是一个非常有趣的教训，因为它也让我们深入了解奶酪如何分类。

segments.en: I personally did not know that you had all these categories of cheeses.
segments.zh: 我个人不知道你拥有所有这些类别的奶酪。

segments.en: Starting out with the soft cheeses.
segments.zh: 从软奶酪开始。

segments.en: That's right, so basically they're broken into these soft, semi-soft, semi-hard, and hard categories.
segments.zh: 没错，所以基本上它们被分为这些柔软、半软、半硬和硬的类别。

segments.en: The soft cheeses are the ones that are actually, you know, you could touch them and they're soft, they kind of move under your finger.
segments.zh: 软奶酪实际上是那些，你知道，你可以触摸它们，它们很柔软，它们有点在你的手指下移动。

segments.en: And the famous ones I think are cottage cheese, which is almost like yogurt.
segments.zh: 我认为著名的是白软干酪，几乎就像酸奶一样。

segments.en: Yeah, and cream cheese.
segments.zh: 是的，还有奶油奶酪。

segments.en: And cream cheese as well.
segments.zh: 还有奶油奶酪。

segments.en: But also ricotta, and brie, and roquefort, and mozzarella.
segments.zh: 还有乳清干酪、布里干酪、罗克福和马苏里拉奶酪。

segments.en: So for example, these cheeses, they're usually, well they're obviously very soft cheeses.
segments.zh: 例如，这些奶酪通常是，它们显然是非常柔软的奶酪。

segments.en: Do you say cheeses or cheese, or chees-eye?
segments.zh: 你说奶酪或奶酪，还是奶酪眼？

segments.en: Yeah we just say cheese normally, or different kinds of cheese, so in that case you make the plural kinds of cheese.
segments.zh: 是的，我们只是说奶酪正常，或者不同种类的奶酪，所以在这种情况下，你会制作多种奶酪。

segments.en: Types of cheese.
segments.zh: 奶酪的类型。

segments.en: So these kinds of cheese, they are recommended, or they say that they pair well with fruits or meat.
segments.zh: 所以这些奶酪，它们是推荐的，或者他们说它们与水果或肉类搭配得很好。

segments.en: So when we talk about pairing a cheese with fruits, or pairing a cheese with wine, what are we saying there?
segments.zh: 所以当我们谈到将奶酪与水果搭配或将奶酪与葡萄酒搭配时，我们在那里说什么？

segments.en: In that case we're saying that it's best to eat with certain kinds of food.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，我们说最好和某些食物一起吃。

segments.en: So you can say, I would recommend pairing this red wine with lamb.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，我建议将这款红酒与羊肉搭配。

segments.en: But in the case of cheese you could say, I would recommend pairing this delicious brie cheese with fruit.
segments.zh: 但如果是奶酪，你可以说，我建议将这种美味的布里干酪与水果搭配。

segments.en: Okay, so you actually have brie with fruit.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你实际上有水果的布里干酪。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: It's, well it depends on the kind of cheese.
segments.zh: 是的，这取决于奶酪的种类。

segments.en: A lot of times you see mozzarella on pizzas, and so it's not paired, it's actually a part of the dish.
segments.zh: 很多时候你在比萨饼上看到马苏里拉奶酪，所以它没有配对，它实际上是这道菜的一部分。

segments.en: It's an ingredient, right.
segments.zh: 这是一种成分，对。

segments.en: But if you're going to eat a piece of cheese alone, you can have it maybe with some fruit.
segments.zh: 但如果你要一个人吃一块奶酪，你可以吃一些水果。

segments.en: So I guess that's the main difference between pairing and having it as an ingredient.
segments.zh: 所以我想这是配对和将其作为成分之间的主要区别。

segments.en: It's pairing, you're combining it, but it's not really part of the dish.
segments.zh: 它是配对，你正在结合它，但它不是菜肴的真正一部分。

segments.en: No, and as an ingredient it's actually, it has to be in the dish to make it work.
segments.zh: 不，作为一种成分，它实际上是，它必须在菜肴中才能使其发挥作用。

segments.en: And so you have a lot of these delicious soft cheeses that you eat at breakfast, or sometimes dessert, ricotta, cream cheese, these are all parts of desserts, like cheesecake for example.
segments.zh: 所以你有很多这些美味的软奶酪，你在早餐时吃，有时是甜点、乳清干酪、奶油奶酪，这些都是甜点的一部分，比如芝士蛋糕。

segments.en: Oh yeah, what do they use in cheesecake?
segments.zh: 哦，是的，它们在芝士蛋糕中用什么？

segments.en: Usually cream cheese.
segments.zh: 通常是奶油奶酪。

segments.en: Oh really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But then you get into these other cheeses which are semi-soft or semi-hard.
segments.zh: 但随后你会进入这些半软或半硬的奶酪。

segments.en: And semi here just means part.
segments.zh: 而这里的 semi 只是意味着部分。

segments.en: So it's partially hard, partially soft.
segments.zh: 所以它是部分硬的，部分柔软的。

segments.en: And these cheeses are different because you might use them sliced on sandwiches, things like that.
segments.zh: 这些奶酪是不同的，因为你可能会在三明治上用它们切片，诸如此类。

segments.en: In this category you have American and Colby, and Monterey Jack is also very, very popular.
segments.zh: 在这个类别中，你有 American 和 Colby，Monterey Jack 也非常非常受欢迎。

segments.en: So these actually do have a more American sound to it.
segments.zh: 所以这些确实有更美国的声音。

segments.en: The American cheese or Monterey Jack, that sounds a little bit different than all the Italian or French sounding cheeses that we had in the soft ones.
segments.zh: 美国奶酪或蒙特利杰克，这听起来与我们在软奶酪中的所有意大利或法国奶酪有点不同。

segments.en: That's right, and you'd even have something like cheddar in this category.
segments.zh: 没错，你甚至会在这个类别中拥有类似切达干酪的东西。

segments.en: There's another...
segments.zh: 还有一个...

segments.en: Cheddar cheese.
segments.zh: 切达干酪。

segments.en: Yeah, there's another good cheese.
segments.zh: 是的，还有另一种好奶酪。

segments.en: As you said, these are very typically put in sandwiches.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，这些通常放在三明治中。

segments.en: Yeah, I mean you can use them in different ways.
segments.zh: 是的，我的意思是你可以以不同的方式使用它们。

segments.en: Sometimes we grate cheese, that means we rub it against this machine, a grater, to make it come out in these little fine pieces.
segments.zh: 有时我们把奶酪磨碎，这意味着我们把它擦在这台机器上，一个刨丝器，把它变成这些小块。

segments.en: For example, on top of pasta or on top of nachos.
segments.zh: 例如，在意大利面或玉米片之上。

segments.en: So we have grated cheese, but you can also have sliced cheese, and that's the way that we cut cheese to put it on a sandwich.
segments.zh: 所以我们有磨碎的奶酪，但你也可以有切片奶酪，这就是我们将奶酪切成三明治的方式。

segments.en: So for example, if you go to McDonald's and you get a burger, usually the cheese that's on your hamburger is cheddar cheese, right?
segments.zh: 例如，如果你去麦当劳吃汉堡，通常你的汉堡包里的奶酪是切达干酪，对吧？

segments.en: That's right, it's a slice of cheddar cheese.
segments.zh: 没错，这是切达干酪的一片。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So moving on to our next category, well actually towards the end of the different types of cheese under the semi-soft category, they also talk about Mexican cheeses such as asadero and queso fresco.
segments.zh: 所以继续我们的下一个类别，实际上是在半软类别下的不同类型奶酪的末尾，他们还谈论了墨西哥奶酪，如 Asadero 和 Queso Fresco。

segments.en: I love queso fresco.
segments.zh: 我喜欢奎索壁画。

segments.en: You've had this before?
segments.zh: 你以前有过这个吗？

segments.en: Yes, many times.
segments.zh: 是的，很多次。

segments.en: What do you usually have it with or how do you pair it?
segments.zh: 你通常有什么或如何配对？

segments.en: Usually it's an ingredient on tacos because it's a little bit crumbly.
segments.zh: 通常它是炸玉米饼上的一种成分，因为它有点易碎。

segments.en: It's like balls as opposed to being one chunk, one big piece.
segments.zh: 这就像球，而不是一大块，一大块。

segments.en: And so we usually have it like that or I've also had it as just a piece of cheese paired with a fried plantain or sour cream.
segments.zh: 所以我们通常会这样，或者我也把它当作一块奶酪搭配油炸大蕉或酸奶油。

segments.en: It's actually very good.
segments.zh: 它实际上非常好。

segments.en: The thing with queso fresco is all of the cheese, they also depend on how mature they are, how long they've taken to make them.
segments.zh: Queso Fresco 的东西是所有的奶酪，它们还取决于它们的成熟程度，制作它们需要多长时间。

segments.en: And queso fresco means fresh in Spanish and this is the main factor in this type of cheese that is very, very immature.
segments.zh: queso fresco 在西班牙语中的意思是新鲜的，这是这种非常非常不成熟的奶酪的主要因素。

segments.en: It's a very fresh cheese.
segments.zh: 这是一种非常新鲜的奶酪。

segments.en: You can make it in like a day or two.
segments.zh: 你可以在一两天内完成它。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: It just takes one night to sit and to become cheese basically.
segments.zh: 基本上只需要一晚就坐下来变成奶酪。

segments.en: But other cheeses, and we'll see some of these in the hard cheeses, take a very long time to become their final cheese state.
segments.zh: 但其他奶酪，我们会在硬奶酪中看到其中一些，需要很长时间才能成为它们的最后奶酪状态。

segments.en: And one of those cheeses is parmesan.
segments.zh: 其中一种奶酪是帕尔马干酪。

segments.en: In Italy, when you buy parmesan, they have these big wheels of it, they're circles.
segments.zh: 在意大利，当您购买帕尔马干酪时，他们有这些大轮子，它们是圆圈。

segments.en: And you have to pay according to how old it is.
segments.zh: 你必须根据它的年龄来支付。

segments.en: Oh, really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: 18 months, 36 months.
segments.zh: 18个月，36个月。

segments.en: And it gets more expensive the older it is.
segments.zh: 而且它越老越贵。

segments.en: So obviously the older it is, just like wine, it has a more intense flavor.
segments.zh: 很明显，它越老，就像葡萄酒一样，它的味道更浓郁。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And there are special characteristics for certain ages.
segments.zh: 并且某些年龄有特殊的特征。

segments.en: Sometimes people really like the young ones.
segments.zh: 有时人们真的很喜欢年轻人。

segments.en: It depends on your taste and what you're going to use it for.
segments.zh: 这取决于你的口味和你打算用它做什么。

segments.en: But Romano is another cheese in Italy that's used like parmesan on top of pastas.
segments.zh: 但 Romano 是意大利的另一种奶酪，在意大利面上像帕尔马干酪一样使用。

segments.en: So spaghetti, you would grate it and you put it on top of pasta.
segments.zh: 所以意大利面，你会把它磨碎，然后把它放在意大利面上。

segments.en: What about, they also mentioned this other one, Asiago.
segments.zh: 怎么样，他们还提到了另一种，AsiaGo。

segments.en: Asiago cheese, Swiss cheese is the one with the holes.
segments.zh: Asiago 奶酪、瑞士奶酪是有洞的一种。

segments.en: Asiago is, I don't know, maybe it's Spanish.
segments.zh: Asiago 是，我不知道，也许是西班牙语。

segments.en: But then we have Gruyere, which is a French cheese and tends to be very, very, very strong flavored.
segments.zh: 但是我们有格鲁耶尔，这是一种法国奶酪，往往味道非常、非常、非常强烈。

segments.en: And I think Gruyere is the cheese that usually many people use for making fondue.
segments.zh: 我认为格鲁耶尔是许多人通常用来制作火锅的奶酪。

segments.en: So they basically have this big pot or this medium-sized pot and all the cheese just melts and you just dip pieces of bread or vegetables in there and you eat this just melted cheese.
segments.zh: 所以他们基本上有这个大锅或这个中等大小的锅，所有的奶酪都融化了，你只需将面包片或蔬菜蘸在那里，你就吃掉了这个刚刚融化的奶酪。

segments.en: Fondue, very popular dish in Switzerland.
segments.zh: 火锅，在瑞士非常受欢迎的菜肴。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But yeah, all these different types of cheese, as you said, there are so many different types and according to the age.
segments.zh: 但是，是的，所有这些不同类型的奶酪，正如你所说，有很多不同的类型和年龄。

segments.en: Now you lived in Italy for a while and obviously they are a nation that enjoy having wine and cheese very regularly, right?
segments.zh: 现在你在意大利生活了一段时间，显然他们是一个经常喜欢喝酒和奶酪的国家，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And I have to say that people in Parma take their cheese very, very seriously.
segments.zh: 我不得不说，帕尔马的人们非常非常认真地对待他们的奶酪。

segments.en: How serious?
segments.zh: 有多严重？

segments.en: Well, a lot of people buy these big pieces of parmesan cheese and they keep them in the refrigerator and you don't just put the parmesan cheese on the spaghetti.
segments.zh: 好吧，很多人买了这些大块帕尔马干酪，他们把它们放在冰箱里，你不只是把帕尔马干酪放在意大利面上。

segments.en: You also break pieces of it and you eat it alone with a glass of wine or some people like to put a little drop of balsamic vinegar on top of the cheese to give it some flavor.
segments.zh: 你还把它弄碎，你单独和一杯酒一起吃，或者有些人喜欢在奶酪上放一滴香醋，让它有点味道。

segments.en: So there are many different ways to eat it.
segments.zh: 所以有很多不同的吃法。

segments.en: I'm sure it's different all over the country, but mozzarella, parmesan cheese, Romano, these are all cheeses that are very, very important in Italian culture.
segments.zh: 我敢肯定全国各地都不一样，但马苏里拉奶酪、帕尔马干酪、罗马诺，这些都是在意大利文化中非常非常重要的奶酪。

segments.en: It's very interesting because, well, obviously we have listeners from all over the world, but some countries have a good culture for wine, cheese and cured meats.
segments.zh: 这很有趣，因为，显然我们有来自世界各地的听众，但有些国家有很好的葡萄酒、奶酪和腌肉文化。

segments.en: Like for example, in South America, if you visit Argentina or Chile, they are a nation that actually have a lot of variety of cheese, wines and cured meats.
segments.zh: 例如，在南美洲，如果您访问阿根廷或智利，它们实际上是一个拥有各种各样的奶酪、葡萄酒和腌肉的国家。

segments.en: But if you take a trip to maybe Colombia, they're not really that type of culture.
segments.zh: 但如果你去哥伦比亚旅行，它们并不是那种文化。

segments.en: They really consume cheese and wine in the same manner.
segments.zh: 他们真的以同样的方式消费奶酪和葡萄酒。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: I wonder if it has to do with the historical relationship between Europe and the place like Argentina.
segments.zh: 我想知道这是否与欧洲与阿根廷等地的历史关系有关。

segments.en: In Argentina, there's lots of Italian former people who came over from Italy many, many years ago.
segments.zh: 在阿根廷，许多年前有很多意大利前人从意大利过来。

segments.en: So that might have something to do with it.
segments.zh: 所以这可能与它有关。

segments.en: Spain has a very strong tradition of cured meats and cheeses.
segments.zh: 西班牙有非常悠久的腌肉和奶酪传统。

segments.en: They have manchego cheese, things like this.
segments.zh: 他们有曼切戈奶酪，这样的东西。

segments.en: So I wonder if there's a relationship there.
segments.zh: 所以我想知道那里是否有关系。

segments.en: I think it's definitely an influence in some way.
segments.zh: 我认为这在某种程度上肯定是一种影响。

segments.en: But the thing with cheese, I think in many places it's very expensive.
segments.zh: 但是奶酪的东西，我认为在很多地方它都非常昂贵。

segments.en: It can be.
segments.zh: 它可以。

segments.en: Comparatively to if you can have a regular mozzarella cheese, but sometimes these other types, they can be very expensive.
segments.zh: 相比之下，如果您可以吃普通的马苏里拉奶酪，但有时这些其他类型的奶酪可能会非常昂贵。

segments.en: Yeah, it's like good wine.
segments.zh: 是的，这就像好酒。

segments.en: If you really want to pay for good cheese, it's going to cost you a lot of money.
segments.zh: 如果你真的想买一顿好奶酪，那你会花很多钱。

segments.en: Now what about this famous blue cheese?
segments.zh: 现在这个著名的蓝纹奶酪怎么样？

segments.en: We didn't mention it, but this is a very famous French cheese that basically has mold on it.
segments.zh: 我们没有提到它，但这是一种非常有名的法国奶酪，上面基本上有霉菌。

segments.en: Well, yeah, all cheese, you're growing cultures.
segments.zh: 嗯，是的，所有奶酪，你正在培养文化。

segments.en: You're growing these things that are alive.
segments.zh: 你正在种植这些活着的东西。

segments.en: But blue cheese, you can actually see it.
segments.zh: 但是蓝纹奶酪，你实际上可以看到它。

segments.en: And it's moldy.
segments.zh: 而且发霉了。

segments.en: It's white and there's some blue or green mold.
segments.zh: 它是白色的，有一些蓝色或绿色的霉菌。

segments.en: And some people love it and some people hate it.
segments.zh: 有些人喜欢它，有些人讨厌它。

segments.en: I think it depends on your tastes, but it does have a very strong flavor.
segments.zh: 我认为这取决于您的口味，但它确实具有非常强烈的味道。

segments.en: Do you personally like it or dislike it?
segments.zh: 你个人喜欢还是不喜欢它？

segments.en: I do not like blue cheese, but I love other kinds of cheeses like camembert, which is a French cheese with a very strong flavor, very stinky cheese.
segments.zh: 我不喜欢蓝纹奶酪，但我喜欢其他种类的奶酪，比如卡门贝尔，这是一种味道很浓的法国奶酪，非常臭的奶酪。

segments.en: So it's not necessarily that it's strong.
segments.zh: 所以它不一定是强大的。

segments.en: It's just that I don't like the taste very much.
segments.zh: 只是我不太喜欢这种味道。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Actually, it's very popular to put on salads, right?
segments.zh: 实际上，穿沙拉很受欢迎，对吧？

segments.en: Blue cheese sauce or a dressing.
segments.zh: 蓝芝士酱或调料。

segments.en: Blue cheese dressing, yeah, that's right.
segments.zh: 蓝芝士酱，是的，没错。

segments.en: It's made out of blue cheese.
segments.zh: 它是用蓝纹奶酪做的。

segments.en: It's a very interesting topic and I'm sure that locally, many people also make or countries have their own types of cheese.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的话题，我敢肯定，在当地，许多人也生产或国家有自己的奶酪类型。

segments.en: I know for example, in Ecuador, we do have also something very similar to queso fresco that's commonly used for breakfast.
segments.zh: 例如，我知道在厄瓜多尔，我们也有一些与早餐常用的 Queso Fresco 非常相似的东西。

segments.en: And here's an interesting thing.
segments.zh: 这是一件有趣的事情。

segments.en: They put it in their cup of coffee.
segments.zh: 他们把它放在咖啡杯里。

segments.en: No way.
segments.zh: 不会吧。

segments.en: It's cheese cheese, isn't it?
segments.zh: 这是奶酪奶酪，不是吗？

segments.en: It's cheese.
segments.zh: 这是奶酪。

segments.en: So basically you have coffee with milk, very popular in Latin America.
segments.zh: 所以基本上你有咖啡加牛奶，在拉丁美洲很受欢迎。

segments.en: And people will take a piece of cheese and put it in their coffee.
segments.zh: 人们会拿一块奶酪放在咖啡里。

segments.en: So obviously with the heat, it won't melt completely, but it will become very bendy and very soft.
segments.zh: 很明显，随着热量，它不会完全融化，但它会变得非常弯曲和非常柔软。

segments.en: And then they'll have it with the coffee and the bread.
segments.zh: 然后他们会和咖啡和面包一起吃。

segments.en: So it gives it a very interesting taste.
segments.zh: 所以它给了它一个非常有趣的味道。

segments.en: It may sound a little bit peculiar, but it actually has a very, very interesting taste, very good taste.
segments.zh: 听起来可能有点奇怪，但它实际上有一种非常非常有趣的味道，非常好的味道。

segments.en: I've had many friends try and they're like, wow, you wouldn't really think that you would probably dip cheese in coffee, but it works.
segments.zh: 我有很多朋友尝试过，他们就像，哇，你不会真的认为你可能会在咖啡中蘸奶酪，但它是有效的。

segments.en: No, it's a very unusual combination.
segments.zh: 不，这是一个非常不寻常的组合。

segments.en: Now what is this special cheese called?
segments.zh: 现在这种特殊的奶酪叫什么？

segments.en: It's called queso de mesa, which is basically a normal, common, everyday table cheese.
segments.zh: 它被称为 queso de mesa，它基本上是一种普通的、常见的日常餐桌奶酪。

segments.en: So it's not any particular, it's very similar to queso fresco, very immature cheese.
segments.zh: 所以它不是什么特别的，它与 queso fresco 非常相似，非常不成熟的奶酪。

segments.en: So I'm very curious to know if in your country you also have a strong cheese culture.
segments.zh: 所以我很想知道在你的国家你是否也有很强的奶酪文化。

segments.en: And if in your country you guys do have a lot of cheese, what kind of cheese is it?
segments.zh: 如果在你们的国家，你们确实有很多奶酪，那是什么奶酪？

segments.en: I know that every country has its own variety of cheeses and some places like China aren't really into cheese.
segments.zh: 我知道每个国家都有自己种类的奶酪，而像中国这样的地方并不喜欢奶酪。

segments.en: So you can let us know if your country doesn't really have that many cheese options.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您的国家没有那么多奶酪选择，您可以告诉我们。

segments.en: So we're very curious to hear about you and your taste in cheese.
segments.zh: 所以我们很想知道你和你对奶酪的口味。

segments.en: Let us know.
segments.zh: 告诉我们吧。

segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。
